page.layout: Running head at top centre above the text; page number top right. Main text in one column with marginal notes in the right margin. Below the text, a copperplate map with its title "Languedoc" set above it, and under the map the continuation of the text in one column. Left margin holds the line numbers 10, 20, 30.

CAP. XXXVI.
Rutenium.
CADVRCIO versus Ortum conjacet RVTENIVM; reliqua claudunt Lang-
uedokij, Arverni, aliique Conregionales Populi. Vulgo Rouargois, La Sene-
fchaussée de Rouargne.
Sedes olim Rutenorum. Ruteni in Itineraria Tabula, apud Sidonium lib. vii. Epist.
vi, Plinium lib. iv. cap. xix, item lib. iii cap iv (nisi alij sint à Prioribus) & Cæ-
sarem lib. i. & vii variis locis, ubi & Rutheni scribuntur, qui Parmeni Ptolemæo.
Senefchallia Rutenensis duas complectitur Dioeceses, cum Vabris, Segodunum Ruteno-
rum; Σεγόδουνον Ptolemæo, vulgo Rodas; Rutena apud Turonensem: Vrbs, quæ multa
ab Gothis, Francis, Saracenis passa, tandem in Francorum venit ditionem. Gregor.
Turonensis lib. ii. Histor. cap. xxxvi & seq. & de Vita Patrum cap. iii. Sunt & alia
Opida: Ville Franche de Rouargne, Gordon, Estanges, Espeiron.
CAPVT XXXVII.
Languedokium.
RESTAT in Tolosani Parlamenti Iurisdictione Major Superioribus, Cadur-
cio Rutenioque, Portio, LANGVEDOKIVM.
Provinciæ nomen; quod Incolæ, reliquis Gallis pro Ya vel Ita Latino-
rum, Oui proferentibus: Oc dicant. Quum capite xv Romanensem Galliæ Idiotis-
mum, ex litteris Nobilissimi Viri Iosephi Scaligeri, in duo summa diducerem fastigia,
Francium, & Tectosagicum sive Provinciale: Francici duas feci Species, quæ vulgo
Oo 2 Langue

marginalia.note: Senefchallia Rutenensis duas habet Dioeceses. Vabrɪ, & Segodunum, hodie Rodas.

page.notes: Map of Languedoc with place names (Lionnois, Viennois, Vellay, Gevoudan, Quercy, Mare Gallicum, Dauphiné, Provence, Foix and others) and a scale cartouche; the map labels are not transcribed. The page-number 435 is at top right. Sidenote "Rutenium" and "Languedokium" headings are set as in print. Small uncertainties in map and marginal text, and in the Greek word Σεγόδουνον, are marked by their print form.
